messages:
Jordan (ACME): Hey team — since last night our Private control plane calls are failing during mTLS handshake. ~60% of attempts return 'alert handshake failure' and our service shows 502s when calling the control plane API.
Alex (Support): Hey Jordan — sorry you're seeing that. Do you have a quick repro command (openssl/curl) and any client-side debug?
Jordan (ACME): Quick repro from our bastion: 
```
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts -tls1_2
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735116234432:error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1524:SSL alert number 48
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=acme-client
   i:/CN=acme-intermediate
---
```
Alex (Support): Alert 48 = unknown_ca. Can you run with -debug and paste the ClientHello bits? Also any corp proxy in path?
Jordan (ACME): We rotated our intermediate last night. The certs chain to our ACME-INT v2 which is in our hosts' trust store. We do have Zscaler outbound TLS inspection for most egress. We opened an allowlist for control.redwood.internal last week but maybe your control plane IPs changed.
Maria (Oncall): If Zscaler is intercepting, it will terminate TLS and present its own cert to your client which breaks mTLS. Two checks: tcpdump to see if ClientHello gets to the server IP unchanged, and openssl s_client -msg -debug to see immediate Alert after CH.
Jordan (ACME): Ran debug. Snippet below: 
```
>>> TLS 1.3, ClientHello, length = 512
>>> extension - supported_groups
>>> extension - signature_algorithms
>>> key_share: X25519
<<< TLS 1.3, Alert, length = 2
<<< 0x15 0x03 0x03 0x00 0x02 0x02 0x28
```
Steve (Neteng): That pattern (alert right after CH) often means a middlebox returned an alert. Either proxy returned its own TLS alert or the server rejected the CH immediately. Does the proxy present a cert to the client? If it does, it likely won't forward client certs to the upstream server which breaks mTLS.
Jordan (ACME): I captured a short tcpdump. The ClientHello reaches the proxy, proxy replies with RST then an alert back to client. pcap shows no upstream TLS handshake to Redwood.
Alex (Support): Ok that points to proxy interception. Two immediate workarounds: 1) Request Zscaler passthrough for control plane IPs (TLS passthrough/no inspection). 2) If passthrough not possible, we can provision a dedicated egress endpoint for you (tunnel) or a different port where inspection is not applied. Which region are you in?
Jordan (ACME): us-east-1. I'll request passthrough but expect change window delay. Can you provide the IP ranges to allowlist?
Alex (Support): We'll confirm exact egress IPs from our side. As a quick sample, our control-plane nodes for your region were 54.123.10.4-6 (please treat as provisional until we verify). Request Zscaler allow TCP 443 passthrough for those IPs.
Maria (Oncall): Also please attach the PEM for client cert and `openssl x509 -in client.pem -text -noout` output. We want to rule out EKU/expiry issues and ensure CN/SAN are as expected.
Jordan (ACME): Uploading client cert and pcap to the ticket. Notes from our logs also show `OCSP: no response` around the same time — could missing stapled OCSP cause immediate handshake fail?
Steve (Neteng): Missing stapled OCSP usually doesn't cause immediate alert unless server is configured to require stapling or revoke-check. More likely the proxy is interfering with OCSP or stripping stapled responses. If proxy terminates TLS, server never sees the client's cert so it can't ask for OCSP.
Alex (Support): Repro steps we asked for: 1) tcpdump on bastion: `tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/mtls.pcap host control.redwood.internal and port 443` 2) openssl s_client with `-msg -debug` 3) curl test: `curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://control.redwood.internal/health` 4) paste client cert PEM and `openssl x509 -noout -text`. Thanks for providing those.
Jordan (ACME): Done. Zscaler ticket opened for passthrough. Their initial response: "we're blocking based on SNI category OTHER_SERVICES and cannot passthrough on 443 by default" — asking for SNI + destination IP allowlist.
Maria (Oncall): For Zscaler you usually need both SNI and IP allowlist. If they rewrite SNI or strip it, then passthrough must be by IP. If they only allow by SNI, ensure your client sends the correct SNI (control.redwood.internal). Can you confirm the SNI in the ClientHello?
Jordan (ACME): ClientHello SNI is `control.redwood.internal`. But tcpdump showed proxy replaced the packet before it hit our MTU, there was a segmentation around 1460 bytes and ClientHello seemed truncated in the pcap. Could MSS/fragmentation be causing the proxy to drop it?
Steve (Neteng): Fragmentation can break certain middleboxes. Suggest forcing smaller TLS ClientHello (e.g., disable large extensions or set smaller TLS ticket size) as test, but the long-term fix is passthrough.
Alex (Support): Next steps: 1) Jordan to confirm Zscaler passthrough for the precise IPs we'll send. 2) We (Support) will verify connection attempts from your source IPs and confirm final IP list to allowlist. 3) If allowlist not possible, we will escalate to eng-runtime for an alternate egress/tunnel option. 4) Please keep pcap and cert attached to the ticket.
Jordan (ACME): Acknowledged — I'll update when Zscaler confirms. Thanks for the triage. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Assigned to eng-oncall
Alex (Support): Ping @Maria (Oncall) @Steve (Neteng) for visibility — marking as P1 until passthrough is confirmed.
